Q: How to use custom framework with third-party framwork in my test ios project? A:

Your framework builds fine alone, but when importing it into another app you get "No such module 'Alamofire'". To fix this issue better approach is:

Use s.dependency in a Podspec
If MyCustomFramework is meant to be reusable, you should create a .podspec file:

Pod::Spec.new do |s|
  s.name         = 'MyCustomFramework'
  s.version      = '1.0.0'
  s.platform     = :ios, '16.0'
  s.source_files = 'Sources/**/*'
  s.dependency 'Alamofire'
end

Then the app only needs:
pod 'MyCustomFramework'

CocoaPods will automatically install Alamofire.
This is the clean, professional approach.

Q: How to add health check for python code in docker container A:

A one-liner Python HTTP GET health check using built-in libraries (no requests needed) returns the status code, enabling easy validation of service availability. It works by opening a URL and printing its status code, which is ideal for monitoring scripts or Kubernetes probes.

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/healthz')" || exit 1
